policy.full_text:
ACME BANK LIMITED
ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING AND KNOW YOUR CUSTOMER POLICY
Version 0.3 (Draft for Board review)

1. Purpose
1.1 This policy sets out how Acme Bank Limited identifies, assesses and mitigates the risk that its products, services and delivery channels are used for money laundering or terrorist financing.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Customer" means any natural or legal person who maintains an account with the Bank or who conducts an occasional transaction through any branch or digital channel of the Bank.
2.2 "Beneficial owner" means the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a customer, or on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted.

3. Customer Due Diligence
3.1 The Bank will verify the identity of each customer using reliable, independent source documents, data or information before or during the course of establishing a business relationship.
3.2 Customer identification records may be verified within 90 days after the account is opened where the branch manager considers it appropriate to do so.
3.3 The Bank will identify the beneficial owners of legal persons only where a single natural person holds more than 50 percent of the ownership interest.
3.4 Enhanced due diligence may be applied to customers that staff consider to be higher risk, based on their own judgement and experience.

4. Politically Exposed Persons
4.1 Accounts for politically exposed persons may be opened by the relationship manager after completing the standard customer due diligence process.

5. Ongoing Monitoring
5.1 The Bank will review customer profiles and supporting documents periodically as resources permit.
5.2 Transactions that appear unusual or inconsistent with the customer profile should be discussed with the line manager before any further action is taken.

6. Record Keeping
6.1 The Bank will retain records of all domestic and international transactions for at least three years after the date of the transaction.

7. Reporting
7.1 Suspicious transactions shall be reported to the Compliance Officer, who will decide whether to inform the Financial Monitoring Unit within a reasonable time.

8. Training
8.1 All staff will receive anti-money laundering training at the time of joining the Bank.

9. Governance
9.1 This policy will be approved by the Chief Executive Officer and reviewed whenever management considers it necessary.

findings.title: Delayed verification window is long and discretionary
findings.explanation: Verification after onboarding is only acceptable as an exception, completed as soon as reasonably practicable and with risk controls. A fixed 90-day window left to branch discretion goes beyond that exception.

citations.quote: this occurs as soon as reasonably practicable

suggestion.text: 3.2 Where verification cannot be completed before the relationship is established, it shall be completed as soon as reasonably practicable and in any case within 10 business days, subject to transaction limits approved by the Compliance Officer and documented risk-management procedures.
suggestion.rationale: Aligns delayed verification with the narrow exception and removes branch-level discretion.

findings.title: Beneficial ownership threshold is too high
findings.explanation: A 50 percent threshold means owners with substantial but minority control are never identified. The standard gives a materially lower controlling-interest example.

citations.quote: more than a certain percentage of the company (e.g. 25%)

suggestion.text: 3.3 The Bank will identify and take reasonable measures to verify every natural person who holds 25 percent or more of the ownership interest of a legal person, or who otherwise exercises control over it.
suggestion.rationale: Lowers the threshold and adds control by other means.

findings.title: Enhanced due diligence is optional and its triggers are undefined
findings.explanation: The clause makes EDD discretionary and does not say which risk factors require it. Higher-risk relationships must receive enhanced measures under a documented risk assessment.

citations.quote: identify, assess and take effective action to mitigate their money laundering

suggestion.text: 3.4 The Bank shall apply enhanced due diligence to every customer rated high risk under the Bank's documented customer risk assessment methodology, including the risk factors listed in Annex A.
suggestion.rationale: Makes EDD mandatory for high-risk customers and anchors it to a documented methodology.

findings.title: Risk rating depends on individual judgement
findings.explanation: Risk ratings based only on personal judgement are not reproducible or auditable. A documented, institution-wide risk assessment is expected.

citations.quote: identify, assess and take effective action to mitigate their money laundering

suggestion.text: Customer risk ratings shall be assigned using the Bank's approved risk scoring model and recorded in the core banking system.
suggestion.rationale: Replaces individual judgement with an approved, auditable model.

verification.note: Source supports a risk-based approach but not a specific scoring model.

findings.title: PEP accounts opened without senior management approval
findings.explanation: Relationships with politically exposed persons require senior management approval and additional measures. Standard due diligence and relationship-manager sign-off contradict this.

citations.quote: obtain senior management approval for establishing

suggestion.text: 4.1 Accounts for politically exposed persons shall be opened only with the approval of senior management, after enhanced due diligence including reasonable measures to establish the source of wealth and source of funds.
suggestion.rationale: Adds senior approval and source-of-wealth checks required for PEPs.

inference_notes: Supervisors in the region have recently focused on PEP onboarding controls.

findings.title: Ongoing monitoring frequency is undefined
findings.explanation: Reviews tied to available resources have no defined frequency, so ongoing due diligence can lapse entirely.

citations.quote: ongoing due diligence on the business relationship and scrutiny of transactions

suggestion.text: 5.1 The Bank will review customer profiles and supporting documents at least annually for high-risk customers, every two years for medium-risk customers and every three years for low-risk customers, and upon any trigger event.
suggestion.rationale: Sets a risk-based review cycle that does not depend on resources.

findings.title: Record retention period is shorter than required
findings.explanation: Transaction records must be kept for at least five years. Three years falls short of the minimum.

citations.quote: maintain, for at least five years, all necessary records on transactions

suggestion.text: 6.1 The Bank will retain records of all domestic and international transactions for at least five years after the date of the transaction, or longer where required by law or a competent authority.
suggestion.rationale: Extends retention to the five-year minimum.

findings.title: Suspicious transaction reporting is not prompt
findings.explanation: Suspicions must be reported promptly to the financial intelligence unit. 'Within a reasonable time' and an internal discretion step dilute that duty.

citations.quote: report promptly its suspicions to the financial intelligence unit (FIU)

suggestion.text: 7.1 Staff shall report suspicious transactions to the Compliance Officer immediately. The Compliance Officer shall file a suspicious transaction report with the Financial Monitoring Unit promptly and without delay once suspicion is formed.
suggestion.rationale: Requires prompt filing with the FIU.

findings.title: No prohibition on tipping-off
findings.explanation: The policy never prohibits staff from disclosing that a suspicious transaction report has been or will be filed. This obligation is absent from the draft.

citations.quote: prohibited by law from disclosing (“tipping-off”) the fact

suggestion.text: 7.2 No director, officer or employee shall disclose to the customer or any third party that a suspicious transaction report or related information is being, or has been, filed with the Financial Monitoring Unit.
suggestion.rationale: Adds the tipping-off prohibition as a new clause.

findings.title: Training is one-off rather than ongoing
findings.explanation: Programmes against money laundering are expected to include ongoing employee training, not only induction training.

suggestion.text: 8.1 All staff will receive anti-money laundering training on joining the Bank and refresher training at least annually, with role-specific training for front-line and compliance staff.
suggestion.rationale: Adds annual refresher and role-based training.
